Nadir

/NAY-deer/ - the stress falls on NAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Nadir means the lowest point something reaches.

The actor calls that year his nadir: evicted in March, dropped by his agent in June, and dressed as a giant taco outside a mall by August.

Worked Example

Morale on the expedition reached its nadir on day forty, when the stove failed, the sat phone died, and the two doctors stopped speaking to each other; everything after that, the leader wrote, felt like ascent.

Nadir marks the single bottom of a long arc — one point, not a stretch of general badness. Astronomers coined it for the spot in the sky directly beneath your feet, the exact opposite of the zenith overhead, and the figurative use keeps that geometry: from the nadir, every direction is up.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rock bottom: Rock bottom is the everyday, spoken phrase for as low as things can go, and it carries a shrug or a groan. Nadir says the same thing from an observatory: it surveys a whole arc — a career, an era — and marks its single lowest point in formal, written English.

low point: A low point is the plain label for a bad moment, and a life can have several of them scattered anywhere. Nadir is stricter and grander: it names the one absolute bottom of the entire arc, the point below every other, in a register built for histories.

trough: A trough is the dip between peaks on a chart, and the word itself expects recovery — another peak is assumed to follow. A nadir makes no such promise and admits no rival: it is the single deepest point the whole curve ever reaches.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

apex: the highest point of anything, from orbits to careers

peak: the everyday word for the top

Where it sits · how deep the downturn goes — dip → slump → nadir

dip vs. nadir: A dip is far milder than a nadir — a brief sag that recovers on its own, nowhere near the absolute bottom.

slump vs. nadir: A slump is milder than a nadir — a bad stretch that can drag on, while the nadir is the single lowest point of the whole arc.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — nadir

Root — nadir: the opposite point (Arabic nazir)

Put it together

Put it together: There is nothing to peel off here: nadir arrived whole from Arabic nazir, 'the opposite point' — shorthand for the spot in the heavens directly opposite the zenith, straight down beneath your feet. Medieval astronomers carried the term into Latin star charts, spelling and all, and English took it unchanged.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Nadir is a loan from medieval Arabic astronomy, and it came alone: no prefix, no suffix, no English cousins built on its root. Its only companion is its sky-chart partner zenith — the highest point, a word you met earlier in this course — which arrived by the same route.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Nadir dresses a low point in observatory robes — use it for the dramatic bottom of a career, a reputation, or an era, especially in writing that steps back and surveys the whole arc. In conversation, rock bottom or low point carries the same news without the telescope.
